hero.title: Physics. Python. Data.
hero.description: Particle physics graduate, trained in data analysis in a research lab. I build complete pipelines, from acquisition to result, in Python, C++ and TypeScript. Currently looking for a technical role.

preview.intro: Two research internships in experimental physics, within groups affiliated to the LHCb and ATLAS collaborations, taught me to build full analysis pipelines: data acquisition, cleaning, statistical modelling, reporting. Python and C++ are my main tools. ROOT, NumPy, Pandas, and scikit-learn are part of my daily workflow.
preview.highlight: This portfolio gathers personal and academic projects: a geospatial simulation in Python, a Python/Qt desktop tool for physicists, and this Next.js website.

full.intro: I'm Samuel. I hold a Master's in Fundamental Physics and a university diploma in Data Science, and I work at the crossing point between research and software engineering. My time with the LHCb and ATLAS collaborations taught me to build reproducible, well-structured pipelines and to make sense of large datasets in C++ and Python.
full.experience: During my Master's, I worked with the LHCb and ATLAS collaborations at CERN, on datasets running into terabytes. It's where I learned to build proper analysis pipelines and to work alongside physicists from all over the world.
full.passion: Beyond physics, I'm passionate about building systems and tools. I maintain a home server infrastructure, experiment with automation, and continuously explore new technologies. This website itself is a personal project where I apply modern web development practices.
full.goals: I'm looking for a role where I can apply my scientific analysis and software practice to real problems, at the interface between research and engineering.
